publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: An authenticated non-superuser may read or modify only items they own. An authenticated active superuser may read or modify an item regardless of owner.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: Determine whether an authenticated active superuser can read an item owned by another user through GET /items/{id}.
premises: At entry to read_item, current_user is the authenticated active superuser described by this task, and the existing item's owner differs from that caller.
requiredResponseDetails: Separate this handler-entry conclusion from any claim that the supplied crop proves the upstream CurrentUser binding.

results.explanation: At the declared-entry boundary, the handler obtains the item with session.get(Item, id), raises only if the item is absent, and then applies the ownership denial only when current_user.is_superuser is false and the owner differs. Under the stated premise that current_user is an authenticated active superuser and the existing item has a different owner, the superuser condition makes the denial control false, so execution reaches return item and permits the cross-owner read. This conforms to the accepted policy, which permits an authenticated active superuser to read an item regardless of owner. The conclusion assumes the stated current_user premise at handler entry. The supplied crop shows the handler parameter and its use, but does not by itself prove the upstream CurrentUser dependency binding or authentication wiring; that upstream proof is outside this declared-entry assessment and is not needed under the stated premise.
